The empty-slice fix resolves the divide-by-zero. The new `first` function panics when `n` is larger than the slice length. That's inconsistent with `last`, which uses `saturating_sub` to avoid this.

draftedFindings.title: average can overflow i32 and has no tests
draftedFindings.body: `sum::<i32>()` panics in debug builds and wraps in release when the total exceeds `i32::MAX`. Summing in `i64` avoids this. Neither `average` (including the empty case) nor `first` has a test, so the empty-slice fix and the `n > len` behaviour are unguarded.

draftedFindings.title: first panics when n > items.len()
draftedFindings.body: `&items[..n]` panics with an out-of-range slice index if `n` is larger than the slice length. The sibling `last` clamps with `saturating_sub`, so callers will reasonably expect `first` to clamp too. Use `&items[..n.min(items.len())]`.
